After  faintiness,  giddiness  and  shuddering. — Br.

Chilliness  over  the  whole  body ;  after  four  hours. — Sch.

Chilliness  became  very  violent  on  undressing,  at  10  P.M.;  after
five  hours. — Sch.

Cold  limbs  with  heat  in  abdomen. — R.Sch.

Nose  cold,  had  to  wrap  it  in  hot  cloths. — R.Sch.

Chilly  while  walking. — Eisenmenger.

With  the  attempt  at  rising  he  feels  chilly,  from  weakness ;  8th
day.— F.K.

Attacks  of  shuddering  or  creeps  in  the  evening,  short,  violent
and  only  on  parts  of  the  back  ;  the  1st  day. — C.Hg,

Evening  frequent  creeps,  with  coldness  running  down  the
body ;  glowing  heat  about  the  chest,  back  and  face ;  later,
general  sweat,  only  not  on  the  right  foot,  continues  all  night,
large  drops  run  over  his  face  and  down  the  head ;  with  it
the  pulse  limping;  8th  day. — F.K.

During  chill :  headache  ;  pressure  in  epigastric  region  ;  disten-
sion of  abdomen;  oppression  of  chest;  tearing  in  neck;  tear-
ing in  upper  limbs. —

With  the  pressing  pain  from  region  of  kidneys  up  to  region  be-
tween shoulders,  a  chill  over  the  whole  body,  with  gouty
tearing  pains  in  the  knee-joints  and  cold  limbs ;  four  hours
after  inhalation  ;  half  an  hour  later,  when  undressing,  the
chill  was  more  violent  than  any  he  ever  had ;  pains  in  the
knees,  upper  arms  and  elbows,  increasing  to  great  violence
after  the  chill;  five  hours  after  inhalation. — R.Sch.

Severe  chill  on  the  3d  day,  3  p.m.,  time  when  headache  was
usually  worse,  beginning  with  yawning,  discomfort,  anxiety
and  chilliness,  accompanied  by  oppression  of  chest,  pain  in
neck,  drawing  in  upper  limbs ;  increased  frontal  headache  ;
after  a  two  hours  chill:  moderate  heat,  lasting  till  8  P.M.,
with  a  hot,  dry  mouth,  but  little  thirst ;  after  the  heat :  very
slight  sweat,  during  which  he  falls  asleep  ;  at  first  frequent
startings,  during  the  unrefreshing  sleep  ;  after  midnight  quiet.
— Eisenmenger.

In  the  afternoon,  3  o'clock,  when  the  headache  had  been  the
worst,  on  1st  and  2d  day,  on  the  3d  day  he  has  gaping,  ma-
laise, anxiety  and  chilliness,  gradually  growing  into  strong
chill  with  constriction  of  chest,  pain  in  the  neck,  drawing  in
upper  limbs,  and  pain  in  forehead;  after  the  chill  had  lasted
two  hours  a  moderate  heat  followed,  lasting  until  8  P.M.;
mouth  hot  and  dry ;  moderate  thirst ;  after  the  heat  some
sweat ;  he  falls  asleep,  but  starts  often  ;  after  midnight  quiet
sleep,  but  on  waking,  weary,  and  as  if  beaten ;  3d  day. —
Eisenmenger.

After  the  great  chill  and  the  fever  on  3d  day,  only  chilly  on
the  4th,  and  on  the  5th  strong  again,  till  on  the  3d  and
henceforth,  every  afternoon  at  3  o'clock. —


117  ARSENICUM  HYDROGENISATUM.

With  the  beginning  of  the  chill  at  3  p.m.:  sallow,  yellowish
face;  eyes  sunken,  listless,  the  conjunctiva  reddened;  nose
and  upper  lip  excoriated  ;  tongue  furred,  yellow  ;  pulse  fre-
quent and  small,  at  the  same  time  increased  headache ;  con-
striction of  chest ;  tearing  pain  in  nape  of  neck  and  upper
limbs  ;  pressure  in  region  of  tonsils  ;  distension  of  abdomen  ;
great  weariness  and  weakness. —

Evening,  5  o'clock  :  fever-heat;  half-past  seven  o'clock  :  sweat,
followed  by  sleep  ;  7th  day. — Eisenmenger.

A  slight  fever  paroxysm  on  the  2d  day. — Eisenmenger.

A  paroxysm  of  fever  on  the  5th  day  more  severe  than  on  the
3d,  after  which  it  returned  every  day.  Cured  by  Nux
vom.;  renewed  on  a  subsequent  occasion  on  inhaling  the  same
gas. — Eisenmenger.

Fever  commenced  at  12  noon :  pulse  up  to  90 ;  did  not  affect
the  head ;  thirst  in  the  afternoon ;  sensitive  to  the  cold
weather;  after  supper  the  pulse  rose  from  90  to  120  ;  6th
day.— F.K.

After  writing  awhile  flying  heat  up  towards  the  head ;  pulse
about  120 ;  every  50  to  60  beats  one  omits,  gradually  oftener,
in  the  evening  every  5th  to  6th  beat,  sometimes  every  3d ;
7th  day. — F.K.

In  the  morning  when  attempting  to  step  down,  heat ;  in  the
evening  cold  feeling  ;  10th  day. — F.K.

Slight  fever,  with  great  weakness ;   5th  day. — Br.

Glowing  heat  in  abdomen  and  cold  limbs  all  night,  with  pain
in  kidneys  and  urinating  blood. — R.Sch.

I  Much  heat  and  burning  in  different  parts  of  the  body,  particu-
larly over  the  renal  region. — F.W.Payne.

General  warm  sweat  after  midnight,  with  a  soft  pulse,  80  to
the  minute,  omitting  3,  4  times ;  7th  day. — F.K.

Attacks  of  night  sweat ;  from  7th  to  8th  day ;  continually  in
the  morning  hours. — F.K.

Night-sweats  ;  13th  day. — F.K.

Night-sweat  in  short  attacks  ;  5th  day. — F.K.

General  warm  sweat  in  the  night,  in  large  drops. —

Sweat  relieves  deadness  in  the  limbs. —

warm  feel  of  such  cases,     d  Collapse  of  cholera.
*^  Attacks.     In  attacks,  as  if  beaten  all  over;  7th  day. — F.K.

On  the  7th  and  8th  day  a  renewed  appearance  of  many  former
symptoms  and  new  symptoms,  and  a  higher  development  of
the  morbid  medical  affection. —

Pains  return  ;  typical  headache ;  after  a  slight  improvement  on
the  4th  day,  worse  on  the  5th,  when  urination  completely
ceased. — Ollivier.

I  Typhus  tertianus  postponens. —

Death  on  the  9th  day. — Gehlen.     Bullock.
